title: Shared telemetry module and config plumbing

tasks.title: Capture the baseline before any edit

details.goal: Record the repository state and the pre-existing check results the plan is executed against, so a later failure is never mistaken for a regression and every diff has a named base.
details.contract: Read-only. Create, edit and delete nothing, including under `.ppm/`. Do not run `bun install`. Bun is not on PATH: every command uses `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun`.
steps: Run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` from the repository root and keep both outputs verbatim.
Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck` and record the exit code.
Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test` and record the pass/fail counts and the total (expected ≈564 tests, ≈47 s).
Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run db:drift` and record the exit code.
Run `ls -a .sangkar/` and `git check-ignore -v .sangkar/graph.db` to confirm the data dir is already ignored.
Write all five results as one block into `ppm task_write_progress` for this task, naming any test that is already failing.
details.verify: Done when the five outputs are recorded verbatim in this task's progress and every command exited 0 — or the non-zero ones are named as pre-existing with the failing test names. A non-empty `git status --porcelain` is reported to the orchestrator, never reverted.

tasks.title: Record types and the three pure record builders

details.goal: One shared module declares the three record kinds with their exact field order and turns an already-resolved context plus an envelope into a record by copying an explicit whitelist, so a later sink or report cannot invent a shape.
steps: Declare `RECORD_VERSION`, the five type aliases, `RecordStatus`, `RecordedStaleReason` and the exported union `TelemetryRecord = CallRecord | IndexRunRecord | SessionRecord` (the one type `report.ts`, its tests and the CLI alias — none of them re-declares it), and the three record interfaces with the exact field order above; type `status`/`total_relation`/`truncation_reason` with the unions from `#shared/envelope` and `stale_reason` with `RecordedStaleReason`, so a typo is a compile error.
Declare `RecordContext`, `CallSpec` (with `suppliedNames`), `IndexRunSpec`, `SessionFacts` and the five exported functions.

Implement `callRecordOf` by copying the whitelist field by field — never spread `spec`, `spec.args`, `spec.suppliedNames` or `spec.envelope` — mapping `stale_reason` through the enum and taking the name set from `spec.suppliedNames` only.
Implement `indexRunRecordOf` including the two rounded ratios and `generation_advanced`.
Implement `sessionRecordOf`, `repoSizeBucketOf` and `rootKindOf`.
Run typecheck and lint, then confirm the file has no `node:` import and no clock read, and that `v: RECORD_VERSION` appears in all three builders.
details.verify: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck exits 0 and $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint exits 0. Done when both are green, `grep -c "v: RECORD_VERSION" src/shared/telemetry/record.ts` prints 3, `grep -c "export type TelemetryRecord" src/shared/telemetry/record.ts` prints 1, `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `src/shared/telemetry/record.ts` (no commit happens between tasks, so the assertion is "no diff reaches a file this task does not own", not "the tree holds only this file"), and `grep -n "stale_reason" src/shared/telemetry/record.ts` shows no assignment that copies the envelope's string without the `STALE_REASONS` check. Note: `tests/telemetry.test.ts` (TASK-006) asserts this module's behaviour; this task does not create it.

tasks.title: Daily-rotating install id and per-process session id

details.goal: An install identifier that is stable inside one UTC day and unlinkable across days, plus a fresh per-process session identifier, both from `node:crypto` random bytes and neither derived from the repository.
steps: Declare the interface and the three functions with the signatures above.
Implement `utcDateOf` from `toISOString().slice(0, 10)`.
Implement the read/parse/compare path so a same-day file is reused.
Implement rotation: mint 16 random bytes as hex and write with flag `"wx"`, falling back to a read on `EEXIST`.
Implement `newSessionId` and make every filesystem error non-fatal.
Run typecheck and lint.
details.verify: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck and $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint exit 0. Done when both are green, `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `src/shared/telemetry/identity.ts` (`record.ts` from TASK-002 is still uncommitted and expected, because no commit happens between tasks), and the module contains no `process.env` read — check with `grep -n "process\." src/shared/telemetry/identity.ts` (no output).

tasks.title: Read SANGKAR_TELEMETRY in config and expose AppConfig.telemetry

details.goal: The consent switch is read in the one module allowed to read tool settings and travels as a value on `AppConfig`, so no other module ever reads the environment for it.
details.contract:
In `src/shared/config.ts` add:

export interface TelemetryConfig { readonly enabled: boolean; readonly dir: string }

and add `readonly telemetry: TelemetryConfig;` to `AppConfig`. `loadConfig` returns `{ enabled: env.SANGKAR_TELEMETRY !== "off", dir: join(dataDir, "telemetry") }`. Semantics to encode exactly: unset or empty string means enabled; the exact lowercase string `off` disables; any other value is enabled (no "0"/"false"/"OFF" aliases — one spelling, documented). `dir` is always computed, so a caller can report where telemetry would go without a second path join.

Update the doc comment above `loadConfig` (currently names `SANGKAR_CURSOR_KEY` as the one setting that comes from the environment) to name both variables, and keep the existing `SANGKAR_NO_WATCH` exception noted in `src/index.ts:590-597` worded as "not a tool setting".

`tests/tools-index.test.ts:108` builds an `AppConfig` object literal; add the `telemetry` field there (`{ enabled: false, dir: join(dataDir, "telemetry") }`) so `tsc` stays green. Do not change that test's assertions.

`tests/config.test.ts`: add a `describe("loadConfig telemetry")` with four cases — unset yields `enabled: true`; `""` yields `true`; `"off"` yields `false`; `dir` is `<dataDir>/telemetry` including when `--data-dir` is given. Test with an injected `env`, never the real environment.
steps: Add `TelemetryConfig`, the `AppConfig` field and the two-line change in `loadConfig`.
Update the `loadConfig` doc comment to name both environment variables.
Add the `telemetry` field to the `AppConfig` literal in `tests/tools-index.test.ts` and change nothing else there.
Add the four `loadConfig telemetry` cases to `tests/config.test.ts`, each with an explicit injected `env`.
Run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/config.test.ts tests/tools-index.test.ts`.
Run typecheck and lint.
details.verify: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/config.test.ts tests/tools-index.test.ts` passes with 0 failures, then `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck` and `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint` exit 0. Done when all three are green and `grep -rn "SANGKAR_TELEMETRY" src/` reports only `src/shared/config.ts`.

tasks.title: Buffered recorder with a bounded flush and a never-throw sink

details.goal: One recorder owns the sink, the identity, the per-process `seq` and a bounded buffer, so a tool call only appends to an array and a broken or full disk can never fail a call.
steps: Declare `TelemetrySink`, `jsonlSink` and `nullSink` in `sink.ts` — one `appendFileSync` of the joined lines, `mkdirSync(recursive)` on first use, no clock and no date arithmetic.
Declare `FLUSH_AT_RECORDS`, `FLUSH_AT_MS`, `TelemetryOptions`, `Telemetry` and the two factories in `telemetry.ts`.
Implement `createTelemetry`: identity, context, the single session record, the stat-based bucket and the git-marker root kind.
Implement `recordCall`/`recordIndexRun` with the `seq` counter, the buffered line plus its UTC date, and `maybeFlush`.
Implement `flush` (group by date, one `sink.write` per group) and `close`, plus the `degraded` on-first-failure path with exactly one warn.
Implement `nullTelemetry`, then run typecheck and lint.
details.verify: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck and $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint exit 0. Done when both are green, `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `src/shared/telemetry/`, `src/shared/config.ts`, `tests/config.test.ts` and `tests/tools-index.test.ts` (phase_0's full whitelist is checked by TASK-007, and earlier phase_0 tasks have already created `record.ts` and `identity.ts`), and `grep -n "setInterval\|setTimeout" src/shared/telemetry/telemetry.ts` prints nothing (no timer keeps the process alive).

tasks.title: Telemetry unit suite: shapes, rotation, off switch, redaction, flush, stdout

details.goal: The module's contract is executable: exact record shapes, daily id rotation, the off switch, a throwing sink, the privacy invariant, the bounded flush and the absence of stdout writes.
details.contract:
Create `tests/telemetry.test.ts` using `bun:test` and `mkdtemp` under the OS temp dir, removed in `afterAll`. Import from `#shared/telemetry/record`, `#shared/telemetry/telemetry`, `#shared/telemetry/identity`, `#shared/telemetry/sink` (`nullSink`, `type TelemetrySink`) and `#shared/config`. Build envelopes with `#shared/envelope`'s constructors and hand-written specs; never call a tool handler and never touch a real database.

Required cases:
1. Shape per kind — `Object.keys(record)` equals the exact field list from plan.approach.md §3 for `call`, `index_run` and `session`, in that order (with `v` second), `v === 1` in all three, and the JSON round-trip is stable.
2. Daily install-id rotation — `resolveInstallId(dir, day1)` then `resolveInstallId(dir, day1 later hour)` returns the same `install_id` with `isFirstRun: false`; `resolveInstallId(dir, day2)` returns a different `install_id` with `isFirstRun: true` and leaves one file.
3. `SANGKAR_TELEMETRY=off` — `loadConfig({ env: { SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "off" } }).telemetry.enabled === false`, while `env: {}`, `env: { SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "" }` and `env: { SANGKAR_TELEMETRY: "OFF" }` all yield `true` (one spelling, case-sensitive), and `dir` is `<dataDir>/telemetry` in every case. The file-level off switch is deliberately **not** asserted here: `nullTelemetry()` takes no options and holds no path, so "it creates no `telemetry/` directory" could not fail — the real proof is TASK-010 Case B, which spawns the shipped CLI with `SANGKAR_TELEMETRY=off` and asserts the directory is absent after the child exits 0.
4. Throwing sink — a `TelemetrySink` whose `write` throws does not reject: `recordCall` returns, `flush`/`close` return, and exactly one `warn` was logged. Assert nothing about the caller's envelope: a `void` method over a copied whitelist cannot mutate a frozen input, so such a case is a tautology.
5. Redaction invariant — build a `CallSpec` whose `suppliedNames` are `["query", "file"]` and whose `args` and payload contain `handleRequest` and `/home/x/secret-repo/src/core.ts`; take `JSON.stringify(callRecordOf(...))`, **parse the line**, and deep-walk every value except the `arg_names_set` array itself, asserting no value contains `handleRequest`, `/home/x/secret-repo`, `secret-repo` or `core.ts`; assert `arg_names_set` is exactly `["file", "query"]`. A substring check on the whole line cannot express this, because those names are supposed to be present.
6. `stale_reason` is an enum — build a `call` record from an envelope whose `read_status.stale_reason` is the `trace` wording, `'"src/core.ts" was last written by generation 3'`, and assert the record's `stale_reason` is `"other"` and that no value of the parsed line contains `src/core.ts`, `core.ts` or `generation`; a second record built with `stale_reason: "root_mismatch"` keeps that value verbatim, and a third with no envelope records `null`.
7. Bounded flush — with 31 records appended and a fixed clock nothing is written; the 32nd writes one line per record in one append; separately, advancing the injected clock by 5 000 ms and recording once writes the buffer; `close()` always flushes, and a flush whose records straddle two UTC dates produces one file per date.
8. No stdout — scope the spy to the telemetry calls only: install the `process.stdout.write` mock immediately before the `recordCall`/`flush`/`close` calls of that one test and restore it immediately after. Never wrap the suite body, because bun's own reporter writes to stdout during the run and the spy would capture it.

Do not weaken a case to make it pass, and do not edit any other file.
steps: Create the file with a `tempDir()` helper (`mkdtemp` + `rm` in `afterAll`) and the envelope/spec builders.
Write the three shape cases against the exact field lists, including `v === 1`.
Write the rotation and off-switch cases with two injected dates and an injected `env`.
Write the throwing-sink case and the bounded-flush case with an injected `now`.
Write the two redaction cases: the deep-walked values with `arg_names_set` excluded, and the `stale_reason` enum.
Write the scoped stdout-spy case, run `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/telemetry.test.ts`, then run lint.
details.verify: `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/telemetry.test.ts` passes with 0 failures and at least 8 tests, then `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint` exits 0. Done when all are green and `git status --porcelain` lists no path outside `tests/telemetry.test.ts` and nothing outside phase_0's own whitelist (the phase's module files are still uncommitted and expected — no commit happens between tasks).
